summary: Catherine Prueitt works in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. She earned a BA from the University of Rochester and a PhD from Emory University under John D. Dunne and Laurie L. Patton, later becoming an assistant professor at the University of British Columbia (attested 2026).
Cathy Cantwell is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Kent (circa 1983–1989) and held a post at the University of Oxford in 2002.

Cecil Bendall was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Cambridge, Oxford, and under Theodor Benfey. He worked at the British Museum, British Library, University College London, and served as Professor of Sanskrit at Cambridge.

Cecil Y. Lang studied at Duke University (~1937–1941) and held academic posts at Yale University (~1949–1951), the University of Chicago (~1967–1970), and the University of Virginia, where he served as Professor of English (~1970–1991).

Chack-fan Lee studied at the University of Hong Kong (~1964–1970) and the University of Western Ontario (~1970–1972). Active in Buddhist studies, he served as Pro-Vice-Chancellor of the University of Hong Kong from 1994 to 2015.
Chaesong Kim is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. Kim pursued doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo (attested 1995) under Yasunori Ejima.

Chagdud Tulku Rinpoche was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under teachers including Delog Dawa Drolma, Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Tromge Trungpa Rinpoche, Khenpo Dorje, Jangchub Dorje, and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.

Chaim Rabin was a linguist who studied at SOAS University of London (~1934–1939) and the University of Oxford (~1937–1939). He held positions at the University of Oxford (1941–1956) and the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (1956–1986).

Chaisit Suwanvarangkul works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held researcher posts at Kyoto University and the University of Delhi, and served as a Lecturer in Buddhist Studies at the University of Otago (attested 2015).

Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad, working in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology, earned a doctorate from the University of Oxford. He held posts at Clare Hall, Trinity College, Oxford, and National University of Singapore, before becoming Distinguished Professor at Lancaster University.

Chamnong Adivadhanasit, active in Buddhist studies and religious studies, earned a BA from Chulalongkorn University. In 2012, he was attested as a Professor of Social Science at Kasetsart University and a part-time instructor at Chulalongkorn University.
Champa Thupten Zongtse is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who held posts at the University of Göttingen, attested in 1991 and as a lecturer in 2009.

Chan Ju Mun is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (2001–2002) and earned a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2002) under Charles Hallisey, John D. Dunne, Morten Schlütter, and Masahiro Shimoda.
Chandima is a scholar in the field of Buddhist studies who studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara under Uma Shankar Vyas.

Chandrabhāl Tripathi was an Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Göttingen (~1957–1960) under Ernst Waldschmidt. He held posts at Göttingen (~1960–1970), the University of Cologne (~1970–1977), and the Free University of Berlin (~1977–1994).

Chang-geun Hwang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 2000, studying under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Minoru Kiyota, and Morten Schlütter.

Changhwan Park is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Otani University and UC Berkeley under Alexander von Rospatt, Noritoshi Aramaki, and Shoryu Katsura. He served as a professor at Geumgang University (attested 2013–2017).

Channa Li is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Jonathan A. Silk (attested 2015) and serves as a Research Fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Chao-heng Liao works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Liao held a post at Academia Sinica (attested 2018) and served as an adjunct researcher at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Charlene E. Makley works in Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Michigan in 1999 under Norma Diamond and Roy Rappaport, and has served as an associate professor of anthropology at Reed College.
